sections.h2: Which Henry County, KY counter handles which tax question?
sections.html:
New Castle has three counters for property tax, and the right one depends on whether you are asking about value, payment or a late bill.

  • PVA: 23 South Property Road, New Castle, KY 40050 (mail to P.O. Box 11), phone (502) 845-5740, open 8 to 4:30. The PVA keeps assessments, ownership records and homestead applications.
  • Sheriff: (502) 845-2909. This office sends and collects the current bill, and the PVA's website links to a bill search.
  • County Clerk: 27 South Property Road, mailing address P.O. Box 615, phone (502) 845-5705. The doors open weekdays at 8 and close at 4, with a break from noon to 1. Late bills and deed recordings go through the clerk, and the office takes eRecording.

The PVA's site explains the January 1 rule in plain terms. Property is assessed on that date, and ownership for tax purposes is fixed on that date too. Buy a house in June and the state bill that year still goes out under the previous owner's name, with the new year bringing the change. The office tries to mail a copy to the new owner using the recorded deed, and a buyer who sees nothing can phone the sheriff.

sections.h2: Why do Louisville commuters look at Henry County?
sections.html:
Henry County is a farm and commuter county in north central Kentucky that has served as an exurb of the Louisville area since the 1990s, partly because land in neighboring Oldham County grew more expensive. The county was cut from Shelby County in 1798 and carries the name of a Virginia governor from the Revolutionary generation.

New Castle holds the courthouse, while Eminence is the largest city. Campbellsburg, Smithfield and Pleasureville (partly in Shelby County) complete the list of cities. The county covers 291 square miles, touches the Kentucky River, and is surrounded by Carroll, Owen, Franklin, Shelby, Oldham and Trimble counties. Every resident counted in 2020 lived in a rural area.

The population went from 15,678 in the 2020 census to an estimated 16,447 in 2025, up 4.9 percent. Two school systems serve the county, Henry County Schools and the Eminence Independent district, so check which one covers an address when you write a listing. The county keeps Eastern time, and the average trip to work lasts 30.5 minutes.

sections.h2: Who lives in Henry County, and who is likely to buy?
sections.html:
The 2020 census put the median age at 42.0 years. Of residents, 22.8 percent were under 18 and 18.8 percent were 65 or older, and the QuickFacts estimate for 65 and over has since risen to 20.9 percent. That older group is the one the homestead deduction below is aimed at.

The same census counted 6,099 households and 6,600 housing units, of which 7.6 percent were vacant. Vacancy among owner-held homes was 1.4 percent and among rentals 5.0 percent. Households with a computer made up 88.5 percent of the total in 2020 to 2024, and 83.7 percent had broadband. Nine in ten residents (89.5 percent) had not moved within the previous year, and 941 are veterans.

Those numbers describe settled neighborhoods where few households move in any year, and a mean trip to work that already runs close to half an hour.

sections.h2: How does Henry County housing compare with nearby counties?
sections.html:
A typical Henry County home is worth more than the typical home in Hart County ($146,000) or Henderson County ($171,900), and three of every four homes here are lived in by their owners.

Households average 2.56 people, and 6,147 were counted for 2020 to 2024. Of adults 25 and over, 86.8 percent completed high school and 15.5 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Employers numbered 212 in 2023 with 1,707 jobs, down 3.4 percent from 2022. Retail sales reached about $259.6 million in 2022. The poverty rate is 15.1 percent.

sections.h2: Who can ask Henry County's appeals board to change an assessment?
sections.html:
Owners can, and so can local officials. KRS 133.120 allows the board of assessment appeals to revise a value when the county judge/executive, the mayor of a city using the county assessment, or a school superintendent recommends it in writing for a named parcel. The Department of Revenue can make the same recommendation.

An owner's route begins with a PVA conference, followed by a written petition at the county clerk's office no later than a workday after inspection ends. Hearings open 25 to 35 days after inspection closes (KRS 133.030), and the board usually wraps up inside five days.

  • Gather land and building details, insurance policies, construction cost, listings and loan papers.
  • Expect a notice and protest date if the board considers a higher value.
  • A taxpayer who listed their own parcel at fair cash value may ask the board to look at a neighbor's apparent under-assessment, in writing and with comparable sales or cost data.
  • Blanket reviews are not permitted.

Payment continues during an appeal. You pay on the value you claimed, and any difference is billed later with interest.

sections.h2: Does Henry County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The PVA's site says owners who are 65, or considered totally disabled, may qualify for an exemption on the primary residence. Revenue Department paperwork sets the 2025 and 2026 figure at $49,100.

On a house at the county's $197,900 Census median, the taxable base falls to $148,800. A birth certificate, license or passport proves age. Disability claims need a federal or retirement-system classification and are renewed yearly, except for service-connected veterans and holders of permanent Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems determinations.

sections.h2: How do I clear Henry County tax debt before selling?
sections.html:
Fold the debt into the sale plan. The tax is a personal obligation of the January 1 owner, and under KRS 134.420 a delinquency lien keeps running for eleven years even after title moves.

Ask the sheriff for a payoff on the current year. For any delinquent year, ask the Henry County Clerk, whose website has a delinquent taxes link. Once claims reach the clerk, KRS 134.119 stacks on the sheriff's fee: ten percent of the tax and ten percent of the penalty. Avoiding that starts with the calendar in KRS 134.015, where paying by November 1 saves 2 percent and each late stage after December 31 costs 5 and then 10 percent.

Deed recording also runs through the clerk, and the seller's transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is collected there. Call the office for current charges.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Henry County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Henry County Sheriff, at (502) 845-2909. Delinquent bills go to the Henry County Clerk at (502) 845-5705.

faqs.q: Why does my Henry County bill name the previous owner?
faqs.a: Ownership is locked in on January 1. A purchase after that date leaves the bill under the former owner until the next calendar year.

faqs.q: What is the Henry County homestead amount?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for assessment years 2025 and 2026, open to owners 65 or older or totally disabled through an application at the PVA.

faqs.q: Who besides the owner can seek a review of a Henry County value?
faqs.a: The county judge/executive, a city mayor, a school superintendent or the Department of Revenue, each by written recommendation naming the parcel.

faqs.q: Does an appeal stop my Henry County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Pay tax on the value you claimed while the appeal runs, and expect a bill for any increase with interest.
